body:
# Independent audit of residue-level Ehrhart mass expansion

**Result: PASS.** I independently checked every argument in
`candidate 57e3e17a84fce5c1`, with special attention
to the half-open cone construction, lower-dimensional lattice
normalization, and the claim that all counted output levels are
actual integer cap fibers. No root proof source was changed.

The result remains an auxiliary mass comparison. This audit does
not infer a simultaneous center or authorize adding bounds from
different residue classes. It also preserves the corrected scope:
arbitrary finite sampling is insufficient for the numerical OC
target; the residue lattice structure is essential here.

## 1. Finite-source expansion

If each source base has the form r+mz_i, its m-fold average base
is r+sum_i z_i and is therefore an integer. The constructed
Brunn--Minkowski combinations are genuine subsets of the output
fiber, even when other combinations produce the same base. The
proof counts distinct bases and uses only one lower bound per
fiber, so it never adds overlapping volume contributions.

The displayed ordered lists in the sumset proof have strictly
increasing functional values inside each list. The last point of
one list is exactly the first point of the next; there are no
other overlaps in that ordering. This gives m(N-1)+1 distinct
sums, including the N=1 case. The positive-threshold level sets
are nonempty on 0<t<a when a>0. Layer cake therefore yields the
claimed mM-(m-1)a without a missing empty-level correction.

If M=0, the desired right side is zero and the conclusion follows
from nonnegativity; the proof does not assert that sums of
zero-volume fibers themselves have zero volume. The counting
case d=0 is kept separate.

## 2. The saturated affine lattice and dilation translation

For a lattice polytope Q of affine dimension s, choose an integer
vertex v_0 and put V=span(Q-v_0). The relevant lattice is exactly
V intersect Z^n. Integer vertices span V over the reals, so this
is a full-rank lattice of rank s in V. A lattice basis identifies
it with Z^s, and this is a lattice isomorphism for base counts,
not an arbitrary affine transformation of the mixed-integer
measure.

Under dilation the affine hull is m v_0+V, and translation by
the integer vector m v_0 identifies its integer points with the
same saturated direction lattice. Thus the counts in mQ are
preserved exactly. Using the subgroup generated by the vertices
instead of its saturation would be wrong in general; the source
explicitly uses the saturated lattice and avoids that mistake.

No determinant correction is needed: only lattice cardinalities
are transformed, while all continuous fiber volumes stay in their
original Euclidean coordinates. The s=0 case is handled separately
as a single integer point.

## 3. Half-open cones really partition the closed cone

The pulling triangulation can use the integer vertices of Q;
neither a unimodular triangulation nor inclusion of every lattice
point as a triangulation vertex is required. The induced order on
each face makes the subdivisions compatible.

The cone over a full-dimensional Q is full-dimensional and
pointed. A vector xi in its interior avoiding the finitely many
simplex-facet spans exists because these spans are proper linear
hyperplanes. For every point w of the closed whole cone,
w+epsilon xi lies in its interior for every epsilon>0. For
sufficiently small epsilon it avoids all simplex-facet spans:
those through w are resolved by the nonzero xi component, and
the other finitely many spans remain on their fixed side. Thus
the selected simplex-cone interior is unique and eventually fixed.

In a fixed simplex cone, let eta_i be the coordinates of xi in
its generator basis. Each eta_i is nonzero. The assigned points
have coordinate lambda_i>=0 when eta_i>0 and lambda_i>0 when
eta_i<0. This proves exactly the rectangular half-open coordinate
description used in the source. The origin belongs to the unique
cone containing xi in its interior, where every coordinate is
closed. It is not lost or multiply assigned.

## 4. Fundamental parallelepipeds and nonnegative coefficients

The generators (v_i,1) are linearly independent integer vectors.
For a closed coordinate, subtract floor(lambda_i), leaving a
remainder in [0,1). For an open coordinate, subtract
ceil(lambda_i)-1, leaving a remainder in (0,1]. The subtracted
integers are nonnegative, and the remainder is an integer vector
because all generators are integral. Uniqueness follows from
uniqueness of the generator coordinates and these remainder
conventions.

Every remainder has nonnegative integer height and bounded height
at most s+1. Its generating contribution is therefore a monomial
with nonnegative coefficient, divided by (1-t)^(s+1). Summing the
disjoint half-open cones gives the asserted generating identity
as a formal power series: every height section has finitely many
lattice points, so no analytic interchange or convergence premise
is needed.

At height zero the closed cone has just its origin, hence h_0=1.
At height one it has exactly N lattice points, so h_1=N-s-1.
All remaining numerator coefficients are nonnegative. Taking the
coefficient at height m and retaining these first two terms proves
the stated binomial lower bound. Permitting numerator degree s+1
instead of proving the usual sharper degree bound does not affect
this argument.

As an independent arithmetic check of the nonunimodular situation,
I counted the dilates of Reeve tetrahedra
conv{0,e_1,e_2,(1,1,r)} for 1<=r<=8 and 1<=m<=6. The exact counts
agree with

    binom(m+3,3)+(r-1)binom(m+1,3),

with the second term zero at m=1. These examples have the higher
nonnegative numerator coefficient which the general proof retains.
I also checked translated rank-one sublattice dilations. Together
these gave 115 exact checks; they supplement rather than replace
the proof above.

## 5. Every level-polytope lattice point is an actual fiber

For a nonempty strict level A_t in the residue class r+mZ^n,
the vertices (p-r)/m of Q_t are integral. If q is any integer
point of Q_t, then r+mq is a convex combination of bases in A_t.
The corresponding actual E-fiber contains the weighted Minkowski
combination of their convex fibers. Each positive-weight source
volume is strictly greater than t, so Brunn--Minkowski gives a
strictly greater-than-t output volume. Thus r+mq is already in
A_t. This proves that Q_t has exactly N_t lattice points, including
all its boundary and nonvertex lattice points.

Next, if q is an integer point of mQ_t, then

    r+q belongs to conv(A_t).

It is an actual integer base, and the same Brunn--Minkowski
argument gives volume greater than t in E_(r+q). This is precisely
the output count needed in the layer-cake integral. It is not a
count of unsampled real sections, nor does it assume that the
original residue class itself contains the output bases.

The affine dimension s_t agrees with that of Q_t. Its saturated
affine lattice counts exactly the ambient integer points in the
relevant affine hull, by Section 2. Points of E outside that hull
only increase the left side. All level sets and dimensions are
finite step functions of t, so endpoint choices at their finitely
many volume values do not change the integral.

## 6. Caps, boundaries, and intrinsic use

For E=C intersect H, convexity and compactness hold for every
closed ambient halfspace, regardless of its orientation. A
vertical cap carrying positive boundary fiber mass is included
exactly in E and in every positive level where it belongs. The
proof omits only zero d-volume fibers from a formula explicitly
about d-volume; it does not reinterpret them as having zero
intrinsic measure.

For the separate intrinsic extension referred to in the D3 source,
the required common-direction argument is valid: positive
q-dimensional input fibers whose positive-weight combinations
land in integer fibers of the original S must have a common
q-dimensional direction space, since otherwise that output fiber
would have dimension greater than q=dim_H(S). Repeated copies of
the same residue input supply the required at-least-two-source
comparison. Translation into that common space preserves H_q,
and the same normalized level proof applies. At q=0 the argument
is solely the lattice count. No undefined 1/q exponent is used.

## 7. Sharp cases and executed verifier

The m=2 binomial simplification and its comparison to 2N-1 are
correct for s=0, s=1, and s>=2 with N>=s+1. The rank-one product
has exactly m(N-1)+1 measured fibers, and the mDelta_s product has
exactly binom(m+s,s) measured fibers. These give the claimed
equalities with all endpoint fibers included.

I reran `supporting computation verify_residue_level_ehrhart_mass_expansion_root.py`.
It passed 7748 exact cap/residue inequalities, including vertical
boundary caps, its equality calibrations, and the additional
triangulation-family checks currently in that program. The proof
of the theorem is the exact counting and cone argument audited
above, not an inference from those finite checks.

No numerical implication for one deterministic center follows
from this theorem alone. Different residue outputs can overlap,
and their separately valid mass bounds cannot be added without
additional disjointness or accounting.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
